title: Sell Mineral Rights in Tippecanoe, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Tippecanoe, OH | Harrison Co.
metaDescription: Tippecanoe, Harrison County sits in the Utica core near where Ohio's early leasing wave concentrated. See what that means for pooled units and offers.
heroLead: The early 2011 to 2014 leasing wave that put Harrison County on the map moved through Tippecanoe and the surrounding townships fast, and a lot of the pooled units formed then are still producing today.
intro: Tippecanoe is a small community in Harrison County, part of the Utica/Point Pleasant core that saw intense operator interest in the play's earliest years. Land near Tippecanoe was among the first pooled into large horizontal units as companies raced to secure acreage positions across the county.

For families who leased land here during that early rush, the original agreement and the unit it was pooled into are usually the two most important documents for understanding what you actually hold today.

sections.heading: Pooled units formed during the early rush
paragraphs: Operators typically combine multiple adjoining tracts into a single spacing unit to drill long horizontal wells efficiently, and your royalty share is based on how much of that pooled unit your acreage represents, not simply your acreage in isolation.

If your land near Tippecanoe was pooled early on, the unit designation and your calculated decimal interest should appear on your division order or royalty statements, which we review as part of any sale.

sections.heading: What years of production tell a buyer
paragraphs: Units formed during the early Harrison County boom generally have close to a decade or more of production history now, giving a clear picture of how the well has performed from initial peak through decline.
That history is valuable when pricing a sale because it replaces guesswork with an actual track record specific to your unit.

sections.heading: Selling a pooled interest near Tippecanoe
paragraphs: We review your lease, division order, and recent royalty statements together to confirm your exact decimal interest and pricing basis before making an offer.
If you are unsure which unit your acreage was pooled into, we can research that using Ohio Department of Natural Resources unit and permit records tied to your legal description.

faqs.question: What is a division order and why does it matter for selling near Tippecanoe?
faqs.answer: A division order confirms your exact decimal share of a pooled unit's production. It is one of the most useful documents for pricing a sale accurately.

faqs.question: My land was pooled into a unit years ago. Do I still own the mineral rights, or just a royalty?
faqs.answer: It depends on your original lease terms. Most owners retain the underlying mineral rights while the operator holds a leasehold interest to produce and pay royalties. We clarify this during title review.

faqs.question: Is Harrison County still seeing new drilling, or is it mostly established wells now?
faqs.answer: Harrison County has both long-established production from the early boom years and continued activity in some areas. We check current records for your specific unit.
